ctx.x: Well, I don’t know. Bud, he would look at you, and he would give you that grimace. You wouldn’t know if he was smiling or what. Bud was very strange at that time. Anyhow, he lived there, and at the time I was working in Birdland with him, Oscar Goodstein said, “Percy, see that Bud gets home,” ‘cause we’re living in the same house. We get in a cab to go from Birdland to the Bronx, and Bud would tell the cab driver, “Hey man, go through 115th Street. Percy, I’ll be right back.” He’d get out [of] the cab, I don’t…

Anyhow, that was one experience we had up there with Benny Harris. We were in a room up in his family’s house in the Bronx at that time. And Percy was supposed to be born a certain week, and being the first child, naturally he was late. So I flew from Chicago, waited, I had to leave back and go back and play with Dizzy, and on Wednesday, Percy didn’t show [until] the next Monday. If I had just waited one week, he showed. So June had Percy there without me, and it was really… yeah, I couldn’t be there, I was in…
